back: English-like, machine independent language; easy to read, write and debug; must be compiled or interpreted.
Machine code or assembly language; relates to one processor's instruction set; allows direct hardware control.
Low-level language using mnemonics (e.g. LDA, ADD), each standing for one machine code instruction; translated by an assembler.
Translates the whole high-level program at once before it runs, producing an executable file; reports all errors together.
Translates and executes one line at a time; no executable file; stops at the first error.
Interpreter: during development and debugging. Compiler: for the finished program (fast executable, source code private, no translator needed).
Direct manipulation of hardware (registers, memory); fast, efficient code using little memory.
Code editor, run-time environment, translator, error diagnostics, auto-completion, auto-correction, prettyprint.
IDE feature that formats code with consistent indentation and colour-coded keywords to make it easier to read.
